summary: David Steindl-Rast is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna between circa 1945 and 1952.

David Tracy is a religious studies scholar and philosopher. He studied at Saint Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He taught at the Catholic University of America (1967–1969) and the University of Chicago Divinity School (circa 1969–2006).

David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale universities. He served as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1972–2002) and taught at Soka University of America (~2002–2004).

David W. Tien is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, where he completed his PhD under doctoral supervisor James Robson and also studied under Robert H. Sharf.
David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Peter Harvey.
Daw Ohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied at the University of Rangoon and served there as Tutor in Pali around 1946.

Dawa Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and UC Berkeley, and served as professor of Central Asian studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University from circa 1986 to 2006.
Dawa Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and held a post at Tibet University.

Daya Krishna was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as professor of philosophy and Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1960–1984) and as chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

Daya Ram Sahni was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Oriental College and the University of the Punjab under John Marshall. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (1925–1935) and as Director at Jaipur State (1935).

Dayong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Taixu, Bai Puren, and Palden Tenzin Nyendrak, taught at Wuchang Buddhist Institute in 1923, and founded the Tibetan Studies College.

Debala Mitra was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Additional Director General at the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961). He founded the Central Institute of Indian Languages, serving as Director in 1988, and chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya was an Indologist and philosopher. Educated at the University of Calcutta under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta, he taught philosophy at City College, Kolkata (~1943–1980), and was a guest professor at the University of Calcutta.

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Harvard under Oleg Grabar and at Vienna. Her career includes posts at UCLA (1978–1985) and the University of Vienna's Asian art history chair (1994–2015).
Declan Quigley is an Indologist who has held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Renmin University of China (~1995–1998) and became an associate professor of religious studies there around 2002.
Demchok Dorje studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga.

Denis Sinor was a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history. He studied under Paul Pelliot and at the University of Cambridge, where he held a post from 1948 to 1962, before serving as Director at Indiana University (1962–1986).

Denis Twitchett was a sinologist and historian. He studied at SOAS and St Catharine's College, Cambridge. He held Chinese chairs at the University of London (1960–1968) and Cambridge (1968–1980), and was an emeritus professor at Princeton (1980–1994).
